about: The posts the town hires or appoints somebody into, and what each department says it employs.

conclusions.basis: Every department report in the annual reports, read for a roster, a stated strength or an establishment.
conclusions.claim: Three parts of the town name their staff. Every other department names none
conclusions.detail: What the town publishes about who works for it, taken as a whole rather than one department at a time. Three parts of the town — the Police Department, the Fire Department and the schools — print every member of staff by name, in every annual report. No other department does. The Department of Public Works states an establishment post by post instead, and the rest state nothing at all — so of the 60 appointed posts the town lists in FY2025, most belong to departments whose staff appear in no published count.

named.unit: parts of the town naming their staff

conclusions.not_shown: Whether an unnamed department is large or small. Publishing nothing is not evidence of either.
conclusions.so_what: Most of the town’s workforce appears in no published count at all.

conclusions.basis: The form each department uses in its own annual-report section.
conclusions.claim: What the town says about its staff comes in four forms that cannot be added
conclusions.detail: Not a single figure anywhere: four different kinds of quantity, chosen department by department. A named roster, a stated strength given as a count and a RANGE, an establishment listed post by post, and a sentence with no number in it. Those are four different quantities and no arithmetic joins them, so this project publishes no town staffing total and there is no honest way to produce one from what is printed.

forms.unit: kinds of quantity, none addable to another

conclusions.not_shown: A town headcount. It is not that nobody has added these up; it is that adding them would be wrong.
conclusions.so_what: Anybody quoting one town staffing number is quoting something nobody published.

grain: POSTS AND NAMED STAFF, never a payroll. One row is one appointed post, or one person named on a department roster. No salary is read or inferred.
not_established: What anybody is paid. No salary is read here, and none is inferred from a post’s name.

How many people the town employs. A DPW labourer, a library assistant and a town hall clerk hold no appointed post and appear in no roster — the wage list that would give a headcount stopped naming departments after FY2016.
FTE. A career post and an on-call post are not the same job and cannot be netted against each other.

A town total. The departments that describe their staffing do it in whichever form that year’s department head chose — a count, a range, an establishment post by post, a list of names — and those are different quantities.
